name: Russian nationalism
summary: Russian nationalism in its dominant contemporary form treats Russia as a state-civilisation built by the Russian people, language and culture with Orthodoxy and the other traditional religions, and holds that Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians are one people. It defends sovereignty against Western hegemony, supports compatriots abroad, upholds traditional family values and rejects an ethnic Russian state, a position ethnic nationalists contest.
scope: The national question only: identity, territory, sovereignty, language, culture, minorities, kin abroad and the means accepted. The mainstream is Putin-era state nationalism (the 2012 national-question article, Valdai and other speeches, the 2021 essay), set beside five other strands: Orthodox church nationalism (the 2024 World Russian People's Council order), Solzhenitsyn, Eurasianism (Dugin), Danilevsky's Slavophile pan-Slavism and the ethnonationalists (Verkhovsky's account). The state's own documents (Constitution, 2023 Foreign Policy Concept, Decree 809) are not counted as nationalist texts. The government's wider economic, welfare and constitutional programme is not counted. Further strands read in the deepen pass: Slavophiles (Khomyakov, Kireevsky, Ivan Aksakov), the state-conservatives Katkov and Pobedonostsev, Dostoevsky, and the ethnonationalist Movement Against Illegal Immigration programme.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Putin's 2021 essay, Solzhenitsyn, the 2024 Council order and Danilevsky's Slavic federation all treat the East Slavs, or the Slavs, as one people to be united.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Putin and the Council cite Russians and Russian speakers who want to live in one Russian state, and Solzhenitsyn would redraw Soviet-era lines to match population patterns, though each adds other grounds.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Putin calls the Russians a people divided by borders, the Council makes their reunification a priority and Danilevsky treats separated Galician kin as a politically crippled nation.

national-self-determination.rationale: Putin rejects Leninist self-determination as a recipe for breakup while invoking it for Crimea and the Donbas, Katkov holds that one of Russian and Polish nationality must give up political independence, Solzhenitsyn accepts it by plebiscite and ethnic nationalists claim it for Russians.

right-to-secede.rationale: Putin's 2012 article and Katkov's 1863 essay on Poland refuse any separation, while Solzhenitsyn would let the non-Slavic republics go and decide Ukraine by plebiscite.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Putin's 2012 article credits great effort with quenching the ethnic wars after 1991 and calls territorial integrity unconditional, and Katkov argues Poland cannot be detached because the Russian nation cannot give up its thousand years and the army underlies the state.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Putin's 2022 speech and the Council order seek the return of historical Russian land and a sphere over Ukraine, Danilevsky and Dostoevsky want Constantinople held by Russia, but Solzhenitsyn urges Russia to shed its empire.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Putin's 2013 speech makes integration with the post-Soviet neighbours an absolute priority and the Council order wants Ukraine in Russia's exclusive sphere, which Verkhovsky also reports as the nationalist aim of an inherited sphere of influence.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Putin's 2014 and 2022 speeches defend Russians and Russian speakers abroad, the Council order makes Russia a refuge for compatriots, and Katkov backed a Slavic Committee fund for oppressed Russian Galicians, as Danilevsky wanted kin across borders joined to the Slavic world.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The 2024 Council order wants conditions for mass repatriation of compatriots and a refuge state for them, and the Movement Against Illegal Immigration programme demands simplified repatriation and benefits for returning indigenous Russians.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Putin's 2012 article rejects a mono-ethnic Russian state as the shortest road to destroying Russia, while the DPNI strand wanted an ethnically homogenised Russia with Russians privileged.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The nationalist texts record no position shared by more than one strand on this question; it belongs to the state's wider programme or to a single strand's views.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Putin's 2012 article proposes a Russian language, history and law exam for migrant status, the Movement Against Illegal Immigration programme demands exams in the state language, history and traditions, and the 2024 Council order requires readiness for linguistic and cultural integration.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Movement Against Illegal Immigration programme demands deportation of illegal migrants, quotas, a ban on hiring unskilled foreign labour and an end to visa-free entry, and the 2024 Council order wants a substantial cut in culturally alien low-skilled labour.

open-borders.rationale: Putin's 2012 article wants illegal migration minimised and flows controlled, the Council order demands controlled flows, and the Movement Against Illegal Immigration wants visas for non-union states and illegal border crossing treated as a grave crime.

multipolar-world.rationale: Putin's 2022 Valdai speech, the Council order and Dugin's Fourth Political Theory present a multipolar order of sovereign civilisations as Russia's own cause.

civilizational-union.rationale: Putin's 2013 speech presents Eurasian integration as preserving the identity of its nations, the Council order says the Russian world is wider than any state's borders and Danilevsky proposes an all-Slavic federation.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Putin's 2021 essay and Solzhenitsyn argue the three East Slavic peoples are one through shared language and history, and the Council order says 'Russian' covers all East Slavs, though Putin's 2012 article also calls the Russian nation a civic whole.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Putin calls the south-west 'historically Russian land' and the Council speaks of the right to live on one's own land within one Russian state, while both also rest the claim on residents' will.

missingStatements.text: A country should regard itself as a distinct civilisation, not only a state among states.
missingStatements.rationale: Putin's 2013 speech calls Russia a state-civilisation, Danilevsky's cultural-historical types and Dugin's civilisations say the same.

notes: Searched all ten themes across the Putin corpus, the Constitution, the 2023 Concept, Decree 809, the 2024 Council order, Solzhenitsyn, Dugin and Verkhovsky. Economy, welfare, government structure, liberty, ecology and technology belong to the regime's wider programme and are null. Strands differ on ethnicity (state nationalism rejects an ethnic Russian state, DPNI-type nationalism wants one), on empire (Solzhenitsyn urges shedding non-Slavic republics) and on self-determination, and those answers are 0 at low. Blocked: Britannica and the OSW analysis (bot wall), the mid.ru Concept page (empty), and Laruelle, Kolstoe and Pain (not openly available). Strand pass (2026-10-30): the state's documents, foreign policy beyond the national question (colonialism, the world economy, deference, intervention, dominated-front) and social policy held by one strand only are null; an answer is kept only where two strands state it, and split (0, low) where strands take opposite positions. Danilevsky's Russia and Europe was read in the 1871 OCR text; Ilyin's, Aksakov's and Khomyakov's political texts were not found openly. Deepen pass (2026-10-30): added Katkov, Aksakov, Pobedonostsev, Dostoevsky, Kireevsky, Khomyakov and the DPNI programme. Not found: Ilyin's Nashi zadachi, Solzhenitsyn's Russia in Collapse, Rodina's 2003-2006 programme (its Wayback capture was an empty news page). Aksakov's 'Jewish question' essay was not used. Review (2026-10-30): democracy-best made a split (0 low): Putin's 2013 Valdai answer backs democracy against the Slavophile and Pobedonostsev line.
